title: Road to Paris
text:
In the morning
        splendors of the sun,
bound for Paris, crossing Spain,
the train stopped in
        a strange little village
that embroiders a river with its slender poplars.


The flowered dawn fills the roads...
and I say to the one who
        accompanies me:
—"There, as shepherd or cane cutter,
I would live gentle crystalline
        days."


But a voice inside me murmurs:
the lake wants to be sea and the
        sea to be spring;
our life is nothing but a vain effort
to find
        happiness in what is unstable;
if you lived there, surely
following the train would be
        your dream!

        Version by Miguel Rasch-Isla
editorial_note: The translation follows Miguel Rasch-Isla's Spanish version and keeps the train-village contrast as restless desire.

title: A Surprise
text:
Today I received your letter. I have read it
with astonishment, for you say you
        are returning,
and I still have not recovered from the surprise...
It has been so long since
        I have lived without surprises!


"That at last you are coming to see me..., that so long
was the separation..." I advise you,
do not come, you would suffer a bitter
disillusion: you would
        find me old.


And like an old man, now, I have called myself
to quiet, and except
        —always the past!—
for one or another memory that on my forehead


puts some wrinkle of sadness,
I cannot complain:
        tranquilly
I smoke my pipe and drink my beer.
editorial_note: The translation regularizes an apparent OCR break in 'always the past' while keeping the old-age resignation.

title: Song in White and Pink
text:
White woman, pink woman.


She comes near me or goes far away.
By marvelous virtue,
she turns into a butterfly for me
in a world of reflections.


White woman, pink woman.


She comes near me or goes far away.
Catching fire, she becomes divine
in the mysterious moon
of the country of mirrors.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the repeated white/pink apparition and the mirror-world transformation.
